page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL40S is a KVM-based virtual server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU provides 8 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics and single-threaded bzip3 decompression both ranking in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression fall into the average range. Memory performance is robust, with PassMark memory scores placing in the top 25%, while large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain average. In LLM inference workloads, the hardware achieves top-tier generation speeds for small 135M models and strong generation speeds for medium 7B models, though prompt processing for larger 70B models is relatively weak.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a qualitative balance between compute cores and high-capacity GPU memory, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial VRAM without demanding massive multi-core CPU scaling. The absence of local storage requires external volume attachments. This configuration is highly suitable for machine learning inference on small to medium models, data science tasks, GPU-accelerated rendering, and specialized single-threaded processing tasks.
